title: Press a full sharps container's cap through a light click to its final lock, then carry it by the handle into a box
instruction: This sharps container is full. Close its cap and press it down until it locks for good, then put the container upright in the pickup box.
context: Closing a full sharps container to its final lock before it is moved is required by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(A): containers are closed before removal so that contents cannot spill. In US clinics this is routine work for about 0.8 million medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092.00) and about 0.6 million licensed practical nurses (O*NET 29-2061.00) (BLS OEWS, May 2025), 1.4 million together, and also for registered nurses and phlebotomists. The O*NET Core task list for medical assistants includes "Clean and sterilize instruments and dispose of contaminated supplies." A full container is a 0.5 kg tub of loose needles and must stay upright. BD's 305487 phlebotomy container has a hinged cap that first gives a light temporary click, then locks for good only when pressed firmly on both sides ('visual, audible, tactile perimeter locks', maker's product page); the maker's instructions say to press down firmly until it clicks on each side, after which the cap cannot be reopened.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the counter top. (1) A BD 305487 1.5 qt sharps container standing open on the counter, centre x 36, y -3: 14.5 deep (x) by 12.7 wide by 22.9 tall with its cap shut, 0.5 kg (filled to its fill line; contents shown as syringes under the clear collar). Red body 15 cm tall, clear collar above it, a moulded handle bar on its left side (y +), 8 cm long, 1.4 cm wide and 1.8 cm tall, standing 3.2 cm off the wall. (2) Its clear hinged cap hangs on a hinge along the front top edge (the side toward the robot), open 100 degrees and leaning 10 degrees toward the robot against its stop; it is a colliding body on a revolute joint with its own weight. (3) Two spring-loaded catch plungers sit under the cap's back edge, 4 cm either side of the centre, 700 N/m each, 8 mm of travel. Pressed 2 mm each they give the temporary click (about 1.4 N each, 3 N at the cap); pressed 6 mm each, with the cap shut, they give the final lock (about 4.2 N each, 9.4 N at the cap), after which the cap is held shut. (4) An open cardboard pickup carton on the counter, centre x 38, y 27: 30 x 28 x 12 cm, 5 mm walls, flaps folded down outside. Nothing else is in the scene; both arms start from their rest pose. A lazy route that leaves the cap shut or presses lightly gets the tier shown in the README, not the full score.
scoring: Read on the state at the end; only the failures latch (a tip or fall, a drop). 0.33: the cap is shut and both catches have been pressed at least 2 mm (the temporary click), the cap still shut at the end. 0.67: both catches pressed 6 mm with the cap shut, which latches the final lock (cap held shut; 9.4 N at the cap). 1.0: also the container stands upright (within 10 degrees) inside the carton with its base on the carton floor, never dropped, and every point over both whole grippers (fingertips, pads, palm and housing) is at least 2 cm from the container's outline (body, handle and cap) while it stays still for 1 s (20 steps). Void (0): the container tips more than 30 degrees from upright or falls off the counter. A container that falls more than 4 mm in one 0.05 s step or 6 mm in three steps, further than the gripper holding it falls with it (a gripper counts as holding it when its fingertips are within 3 mm of the container and it falls to within 5 mm of the container's fall), is capped at 0.67; a descent in hand is not a drop. Real trial (the 2, 6, 3, 4 and 5 mm readings and the 6 mm three-step limit are sim-only): the first click (cap shut) and the second, firmer click are heard or seen on the filmed trial; the cap is pulled by hand afterwards and stays locked with both tabs engaged; a photo shows the container upright in the carton; both grippers are off it and still for 1 s; no free fall after release. Two named cameras (front and overhead) film it. Fill the real container with new needle-free syringes, not discarded ones.
run_limit: 1,600 steps (80 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches 1.0 in about 575 steps (29 s) on an RTX 3090 Ti.
reset_notes: About 30 s, nothing consumed: take the container out of the carton, stand it on the counter, swing the cap open until it rests on its stop and press the catches back up. Nothing is random; no seed changes the scene.
fidelity: BD 305487 at its true outer size (127 x 145 x 229 mm), 0.5 kg. Estimates: mass, catch spring 700 N/m, 2 and 6 mm click depths, 3 N and 9.4 N press forces (no real container was measured). Cap is a rigid hinged body, so both catches go down together; the final lock's snap is code holding the hinge once both catches are 6 mm down. Contents are a visual insert; the carton is a fixed body; arm links beyond the gripper are not in the clearance test.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (1 trial, 1,600 steps, session held); demo: 1.0
